entries.ex: Technological *innovation* has transformed the way people learn and work.
entries.exAr: غيّر *الابتكار* التكنولوجي طريقة تعلّم الناس وعملهم.

entries.ex: Many students now bring a mobile *device* to every lecture.
entries.exAr: يُحضر كثير من الطلاب الآن *جهازًا* محمولًا إلى كل محاضرة.

entries.ex: Schools must update their *software* regularly to protect students' personal information.
entries.exAr: يجب على المدارس تحديث *برمجياتها* بانتظام لحماية المعلومات الشخصية للطلاب.

entries.ex: Replacing old *hardware* can be expensive for small businesses.
entries.exAr: قد يكون استبدال *العتاد* القديم مكلفًا للشركات الصغيرة.

entries.ex: *Artificial intelligence* is increasingly used to detect diseases in medical scans.
entries.exAr: يزداد استخدام *الذكاء الاصطناعي* للكشف عن الأمراض في الصور الطبية.

entries.ex: *Automation* in factories has reduced the need for manual labour.
entries.exAr: قلّلت *الأتمتة* في المصانع الحاجة إلى العمل اليدوي.

entries.ex: Libraries are turning their old collections into *digital* archives.
entries.exAr: تحوّل المكتبات مجموعاتها القديمة إلى أرشيفات *رقمية*.

entries.ex: Hospitals keep patient records in a secure *database*.
entries.exAr: تحتفظ المستشفيات بسجلات المرضى في *قاعدة بيانات* آمنة.

entries.ex: The university's computer *network* crashed in the middle of the online exam.
entries.exAr: تعطّلت *شبكة* الحاسوب في الجامعة في منتصف الامتحان الإلكتروني.

entries.ex: Most cafés and airports now offer free *wireless* internet access.
entries.exAr: تقدّم معظم المقاهي والمطارات الآن خدمة إنترنت *لاسلكية* مجانية.

entries.ex: Teenagers often want the latest *gadget* as soon as it appears in the shops.
entries.exAr: غالبًا ما يرغب المراهقون في أحدث *جهاز إلكتروني* فور ظهوره في المتاجر.

entries.ex: Many smartphones become *obsolete* within just a few years.
entries.exAr: تصبح كثير من الهواتف الذكية *متقادمة* في غضون سنوات قليلة فقط.

entries.ar: متطور جدًا، أحدث ما توصلت إليه التقنية
entries.ex: The new hospital is equipped with *cutting-edge* medical equipment.
entries.exAr: المستشفى الجديد مجهّز بمعدات طبية *متطورة جدًا*.

entries.ex: Older people tend to prefer simple, *user-friendly* apps.
entries.exAr: يميل كبار السن إلى تفضيل التطبيقات البسيطة *السهلة الاستخدام*.

entries.ex: Students can *download* lecture notes from the university website.
entries.exAr: يستطيع الطلاب *تنزيل* ملاحظات المحاضرات من موقع الجامعة.

entries.ex: Many people *browse* the internet for hours without noticing the time.
entries.exAr: *يتصفّح* كثير من الناس الإنترنت لساعات دون أن يلاحظوا مرور الوقت.

entries.ex: Users are increasingly worried about their *privacy* on social media.
entries.exAr: يزداد قلق المستخدمين على *خصوصيتهم* في وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي.

entries.ex: Companies collect huge amounts of *data* about customers' shopping habits.
entries.exAr: تجمع الشركات كميات هائلة من *البيانات* عن عادات العملاء في التسوق.

entries.ex: Search engines rely on a complex *algorithm* to rank web pages.
entries.exAr: تعتمد محركات البحث على *خوارزمية* معقدة لترتيب صفحات الويب.

entries.ex: Trainee pilots can practise emergency landings in a *virtual* environment.
entries.exAr: يستطيع الطيارون المتدربون التدرّب على الهبوط الاضطراري في بيئة *افتراضية*.

entries.ex: *Interactive* whiteboards make lessons more engaging for young learners.
entries.exAr: تجعل السبورات *التفاعلية* الدروس أكثر تشويقًا للمتعلمين الصغار.

entries.ex: Doctors advise parents to limit their children's *screen time* to two hours a day.
entries.exAr: ينصح الأطباء الآباء بتحديد *وقت استخدام الشاشات* لأطفالهم بساعتين يوميًا.

entries.ex: Some argue that *surveillance* cameras in city centres help to reduce street crime.
entries.exAr: يرى بعضهم أن كاميرات *المراقبة* في وسط المدن تساعد على الحد من جرائم الشوارع.

entries.ex: A *hacker* stole the personal details of thousands of bank customers.
entries.exAr: سرق *قرصان إلكتروني* البيانات الشخصية لآلاف من عملاء البنك.

entries.ex: Online banks use strong *encryption* to keep transactions secure.
entries.exAr: تستخدم البنوك الإلكترونية *تشفيرًا* قويًا للحفاظ على أمان المعاملات.

entries.ex: In modern warehouses, a single *robot* can sort thousands of parcels an hour.
entries.exAr: في المستودعات الحديثة، يستطيع *روبوت* واحد فرز آلاف الطرود في الساعة.

entries.ex: Cloud *storage* allows people to access their files from any device.
entries.exAr: يتيح *التخزين* السحابي للناس الوصول إلى ملفاتهم من أي جهاز.

entries.ex: The company plans to *upgrade* all its computers before the end of the year.
entries.exAr: تخطط الشركة *لتحديث* جميع حواسيبها قبل نهاية العام.

entries.ex: This app is not *compatible* with older versions of the operating system.
entries.exAr: هذا التطبيق غير *متوافق* مع الإصدارات القديمة من نظام التشغيل.

entries.ex: Because of the *digital divide*, poorer families often lack reliable internet access.
entries.exAr: بسبب *الفجوة الرقمية*، كثيرًا ما تفتقر الأسر الأفقر إلى اتصال موثوق بالإنترنت.

gap.s: Without regular updates, many devices quickly become ____.
Governments must protect citizens' ____ when they collect personal information online.
The rise of ____ in car factories has led to fewer jobs on assembly lines.
Before installing the program, check that it is ____ with your computer.
Strong ____ makes it almost impossible for criminals to read stolen messages.
Most offices ____ their computer systems every few years to improve security.
Critics argue that constant ____ of employees' emails damages trust in the workplace.
Countries that invest heavily in research tend to lead the world in ____.

para.a: The laboratory has the newest and most advanced equipment.
para.b: The laboratory is equipped with *cutting-edge* technology.

para.a: Some people do not have computers or the internet at home.
para.b: The *digital divide* leaves many households without access to computers or the internet.

para.a: This website is very easy for anyone to use.
para.b: The website is highly *user-friendly*, even for first-time visitors.

para.a: Children spend too many hours looking at phones and tablets.
para.b: Excessive *screen time* on phones and tablets is common among children.

p1.q: How often do you use the internet?
p1.a: Almost constantly, to be honest. I *browse* news websites over breakfast, check emails on my phone on the way to work, and in the evening I usually watch a documentary or talk to relatives online.

p1.q: Do you prefer reading on paper or on a screen?
p1.a: I'd say paper, mainly because my eyes get tired after hours on a laptop. That said, a *digital* copy is far more convenient when I'm travelling, since I can carry hundreds of books on one small *device*.

p1.q: Is there a gadget you couldn't live without?
p1.a: Probably my smartphone. It's not just a phone; it's my camera, my map and my diary. I've thought about reducing my *screen time*, but honestly, it would be hard to give up such a useful *gadget*.

p2.cue: Describe a piece of technology that you find useful.
points: and explain why you find it so useful
p2.a: I'd like to talk about my laptop, which is probably the most useful piece of technology I own. I bought it about three years ago, just before I started my master's degree, because my old computer had become almost *obsolete* and kept crashing. I use it for nearly everything. During the day, I write reports, join video meetings and access my university's online *database* of journal articles. In the evening, I sometimes watch lectures or *download* podcasts to listen to on the bus. It's light, the battery lasts all day, and the *software* is very *user-friendly*, so I rarely need anyone's help. The main reason I find it so useful is that it gives me freedom. I can work from home, from a library or even from a café with *wireless* access, and all my files are backed up in cloud *storage*, so I never worry about losing my work. In short, it has made me far more productive and independent.

p3.q: Do you think artificial intelligence will replace human workers in the future?
p3.a: To some extent, yes. *Automation* has already taken over many repetitive jobs in factories and warehouses, and *artificial intelligence* is now moving into areas such as customer service and translation. However, I believe jobs that require empathy, creativity and complex judgement, like nursing or teaching, will remain largely human. The real challenge for governments is retraining workers whose roles disappear.

p3.q: Should governments be allowed to monitor what people do online?
p3.a: I think a limited amount of monitoring is justified, for example to track suspected criminals or prevent serious crime. But mass *surveillance* of ordinary citizens is a real threat to *privacy*. If people feel they are always being watched, they may stop expressing their opinions freely. So any monitoring should be strictly controlled by law and overseen by independent courts.

writing.q: Many children now spend several hours a day using computers, tablets and smartphones. Some people believe this has a negative effect on their development. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay: In the past decade, smartphones and tablets have become a normal part of childhood, and many young people now spend several hours a day in front of a screen. While I accept that technology offers some genuine benefits, I largely agree that excessive *screen time* harms children's development.

The most obvious concern is physical health. Children who spend their free time watching videos or playing games are far more likely to lead inactive lives, which increases the risk of obesity and poor eyesight. Moreover, using a *device* late at night can disturb sleep, leaving pupils tired and unable to concentrate at school. Social skills may also suffer, since a child chatting in a *virtual* world has fewer opportunities to learn how to read facial expressions or resolve disagreements face to face.

That said, technology is not harmful in itself. *Interactive* learning apps can make subjects such as mathematics more enjoyable, and online research teaches children how to find and evaluate information. In a world increasingly shaped by *artificial intelligence* and *automation*, young people who lack basic *digital* skills will be at a disadvantage in the job market. The problem, therefore, lies not in the screens themselves but in how long and how wisely they are used.

In conclusion, although screens can support learning and prepare children for the future, spending too many hours on them damages their health, sleep and social development. Parents and schools should therefore set clear limits and encourage a healthy balance between online and offline activities, such as reading, sport and time with family.
writing.tipAr: في مقال الرأي، اذكر موقفك بوضوح في المقدمة وأكّده في الخاتمة، وناقش الرأي المخالف في فقرة واحدة ثم بيّن لماذا يبقى رأيك أقوى.
